text: The chapter uses the matrix [[0, 10], [0, 0]] to illustrate that:
choices: a matrix can have spectral radius rho = 0 while its spectral norm sigma_max = 10, so the spectral-norm condition is overly conservative
the spectral radius always equals the largest singular value for triangular matrices
raising the connectivity pushes the spectral radius above the spectral norm
a spectral radius above 1 guarantees the ESP fails for every bounded input
explanation: This nilpotent matrix has both eigenvalues equal to 0 (rho = 0) but sigma_max = 10, so ||W||_2 < 1 would reject it even though it trivially satisfies the ESP (W^2 = 0). It shows the gap rho <= sigma_max for non-normal matrices and why the spectral-norm rule is overcautious. It does not show rho = sigma_max (they differ here), says nothing about connectivity, and actually demonstrates the OPPOSITE of option D (large sigma_max/rho need not break the ESP).
